provider: LANDFIRE / U.S. Geological Survey and U.S. Forest Service
api_version: LANDFIRE Product Service (LFPS) with versioned 2025 data releases

request_contract.parameter_rules: Documentation-only record of official LFPS REST entry point. Do not create asynchronous layer export jobs, request raster assets, submit bounding boxes, arbitrary output projections, spatial selections or user-supplied URL/paths/headers. Only after an exact endpoint, source product (such as FBFM40), region, release, output resolution, upstream licence and bounded response envelope are reviewed may a separate active probe be defined.

response_contract.format: LANDFIRE LFPS service documentation/entry page only; not a raster or task response.
response_contract.scientific_semantics: LANDFIRE 2025 includes regional, product-specific fuel classes, vegetation characteristics, canopy data and disturbance layers released on a phased schedule. They are derived mapping products, not observed event footprints, ignition rates, building vulnerability or insured losses; preserve product name, edition, units, geography and epoch.

operational_constraints.rate_limit_notes: Provider documents LFPS REST with asynchronous exports; no requests or jobs are authorized here and provider concurrency/export limits remain unreviewed.
operational_constraints.mutability_notes: The 2025 releases are phased by area and product; availability may differ from other LANDFIRE years and exact source bytes must be versioned at future admission.

rights_and_policy.notes: USGS and Forest Service publication and public access do not by themselves establish exact release-specific terms, automated service quota, licensing for every derived layer or permission to rehost output. A separate rights and product review is required.

notes: T0 documentation-only LFPS entry-point contract. No API endpoint for an individual product, no asynchronous job, no original raster or SHA-stamped sample receipt was acquired. Future CAT use requires exact product/version, scientific role and external data-byte provenance.
